title: `project_file_unwritable` can claim nothing changed after an earlier write landed
description: Found while fixing WCLI-7 (the review's F4 class, one step further out). src/contract/errors.ts declares project_file_unwritable as 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Nothing was changed.' A single-target run makes that true, but ward init writes the manifest and then each selected bridge file, and the write of a later target can fail (unwritable or read-only file, a write error) after an earlier one has landed via temp-file-and-rename. The error then reports that nothing was changed while a file in the repository has, in fact, changed. Not fixed in WCLI-7 because it changes a user-facing contract string outside that task's review fix list; recorded here rather than left silent. Related and deliberately NOT in scope: whether the fix is a truthful rewording or a reordering is a design decision, and the same question applies to any multi-file command that reports a single 'nothing changed' claim.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The message a failed multi-file write reports is true in every path that raises it: a test makes the second of two targets unwritable after the first has been written, and asserts the reported text does not claim that nothing was changed (and documents what it does claim)

No other error in the catalog carries an unqualified nothing-was-changed claim in a path that can follow a successful write; each is either verified single-target or reworded, and the audit is recorded in the task notes
